title: Automated batching/cache recommendation pipeline with safe apply and regression harness
creator: Aisha Khatri
description: Build an automated pipeline that recommends batching and KV-prefix caching configurations per model+route, safely applies those configs to serving fleets through a canaryed rollout, and validates no meaningful quality regression via an automated eval harness (golden prompts + workload-sampled suites). The pipeline should: 1) ingest telemetry (latency, tokens-per-request, sequence-length distribution) and cost signals, 2) produce a ranked set of candidate config changes (batch size ranges, cache ttl/prefix rules, quantization hints), 3) validate candidates in a shadow/canary environment using golden prompts and sampled customer workloads, 4) block or auto-rollback if acceptance thresholds are not met, and 5) emit observability and post-mortem artifacts for manual review. Goal: 10-25% median cost/unit reduction for eligible routes with <=1% customer-facing quality regressions on defined acceptance metrics.
acceptance_criteria: Pipeline generates candidate config recommendations with expected cost delta and estimated latency impact for >=80% of high-volume routes
Canary apply path runs candidates on 1% traffic shadow for 1 hour and executes full eval harness before promote

Eval harness includes golden prompt suite, sampled production prompts, and adversarial permutations; thresholds enforce max -1% relative drop on primary utility metric and max +0.5% hallucination-rate increase
Automatic rollback triggers when any threshold is breached during canary or in first 24h of promotion
Dashboard shows per-route before/after cost, latency P50/P95, and eval-harness pass/fail with links to failing examples
implementation_notes: Recommendation engine: use lightweight heuristic + ML model that predicts cost vs latency trade-off from recent telemetry (start heuristic, iterate ML later)
Shadow testing: duplicate incoming requests to canary pods with sampled tokens but block responses to customers; collect predicted outputs for eval
Eval harness: compute utility_score (task-specific), n-gram overlap (ROUGE/ROUGE-L where applicable), and hallucination detector score; unify into single pass/fail decision with per-metric guardrails
Canary rollout plan: 1% shadow -> 0.5% live mirror -> 5% live gradual increase with 30m evaluation windows; abort/rollback thresholds at each step
Store golden prompts and baseline outputs in versioned S3 folder with hash; tie each candidate to a baseline commit id for reproducibility
risks: False negatives in eval harness: risk that golden prompts do not cover subtle regression modes leading to customer impact
Latency spikes: larger batch sizes can reduce cost but increase tail latency; must ensure P95 SLOs not violated for low-latency routes
Data drift: model response distribution may change causing previously safe cache settings to misbehave
Automation blast radius: auto-apply without conservative throttles could affect many customers if safeguards fail
updates: 2026-02-12 - Aisha Khatri: Kickoff meeting with SRE, Runtime and Eval teams. Agreed scope: start with text-generation routes that exceed 2k tokens/day and P50 latency <250ms.
2026-02-20 - Miguel Ortega: Prototype recommendation heuristics completed; naive rule: if median seq_len < 128 and tokens_per_req > 60 -> suggest batch_size 16-32 and enable prefix cache TTL 60s
2026-02-27 - Design review (Lina Park): Observability dashboard mockups reviewed; added quick-filter by customer tier and model family
2026-03-03 - Eval team (Rohit Mehta): Assembled golden prompt set (420 prompts) with per-task expected outputs. Baseline run completed against runtime-1.21 commit abc123
2026-03-06 - Miguel Ortega: Implemented shadowing infrastructure and data capture; shadow traffic uses sampling reservoir to keep cost bounded
2026-03-09 - SRE (Holly Chen): Canary orchestration policy added to autoscaler to support 3-phase rollout and automated rollback webhooks

2026-03-12 - QA (Sandeep Rao): Early harness runs show two failure modes: (1) for one summarization model, batching increased beam-search non-determinism causing ROUGE-L drop of 1.8% on long-doc golden prompts, (2) KV-cache TTL=300s caused stale prefix reuse for a multi-turn chat flow leading to context bleed in ~0.3% cases. Filed follow-ups under ENG-20512 and ENG-20513
qa_plan: Run full eval harness on every candidate in shadow for minimum 1 hour and 10k sampled prompts
Include adversarial permutations: shuffled user-system turns, truncated prompts, injected instructions to test hallucination regression
Comparison baseline: pairwise diff against stored baseline outputs and compute per-example signal (utility delta, hallucination score delta)
Manual review by Eval SMEs for any candidate failing by >0.5% on primary metric before human-blocked auto-rollback is considered
Post-promotion sampling: audit a 0.1% of real responses with automated monitors for drift for first 72h
rollback_plan: Immediate rollback on canary if any primary acceptance threshold crossed; rollback enacted by orchestration webhook and creates incident ticket
If regression detected post-promotion (first 24h), automatically scale down new config to previous and notify affected customers and CS
Automated data capture: keep payloads, baseline and candidate outputs, and eval metrics to support RCA
Human-in-the-loop: require SRE + Product signoff if automated rollback is suppressed for investigation
Postmortem template: include failure delta table, top 10 failing examples, timeline of rollout, and remediation actions
